daily.title: RBI gold share in forex reserves falls below 14% after price correction
daily.summary: Gold’s share in India’s forex reserves fell to 13.98% by November 13, as prices dropped from their January peak while RBI gold holdings stayed nearly unchanged. Gold’s share in India’s foreign exchange reserves has fallen below 14 per cent, reaching its lowest level since September 26, 2025, as the international price of the precious metal fell from its January 2026 peak. Businessline analysis of RBI data shows gold’s share of total foreign exchange reserves climbed from 13.57 per cent on September 26, 2025, to a peak of 19.02 per cent on January 30, 2026.

daily.title: Section 153C Assessments Quashed for Eight-Month Delay in Recording Satisfaction: ITAT Delhi
daily.summary: ITAT Delhi quashes Section 153C assessments for three years as satisfaction was recorded eight months after completion of the searched person’s assessments. Summary: In Abhishek Malik v. DCIT , ITA Nos. 4509, 4568 and 4577/Del/2025 , the Delhi ITAT held that a satisfaction note recorded about eight months after completion of the searched person’s assessments could not be regarded as having been recorded immediately after their completion. The Tribunal accordingly quashed the proceedings under section 153C for AYs 2016–17, 2017–18 and 2018–19 .

daily.title: Customs: Penalties on customs broker set aside where no knowledge of export overvaluation shown - CESTAT New Delhi
daily.summary: CESTAT New Delhi sets aside penalties on a customs broker, ruling no knowledge of export overvaluation was proven. Learn more about this significant ruling. Brief : A customs broker filed export shipping bills for an exporter whose goods were later found overvalued, and penalties under sections 114(iii) and 114AA of the Customs Act, 1962 were imposed on the broker and upheld by the Commissioner (Appeals). The Tribunal held that the Revenue had brought no evidence that the broker knew of the overvaluation, and no proceedings had been initiated against the broker under the Customs Brokers Licensing Regulations, 2018.

Brief : Revenue demanded service tax of about Rs. 89.82 lakh on penalty and liquidated damages collected by the respondent from contractors, treating it as a declared service under section 66E(e) of the Finance Act, 1994. The Commissioner (Appeals) set aside the demand relying on an earlier Tribunal decision. Revenue argued that the Supreme Court appeal against that decision was pending.

breaking.title: SEBI opens non-agricultural commodity derivatives to FPIs
breaking.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India – SEBI has permitted foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) to participate in physically (non-cash) settled non-agricultural commodity derivative contracts. In a circular issued today, SEBI said the move is aimed at deepening institutional participation and enhancing liquidity in the commodity derivatives segment. Currently, FPIs are permitted to participate in the commodity derivatives segment of recognised stock exchanges only through cash-settled non-agricultural commodity derivative contracts. The new framework, will however allow FPIs to trade in non-cash settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives, excluding options in goods, subject to specified safeguards.
